rows.name: Cursor desktop editor
rows.reason: Its documentation requires migrating settings into Cursor, a separate VS Code-based editor, so it fails the request to work directly inside VS Code.

rows.name: Continue with a local Ollama backend
rows.reason: Continue connects VS Code to local Ollama models for completion, chat and editing. Hardware/model quality limit practicality; reliable agent mode additionally requires working tool support.

rows.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
rows.reason: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct has Cline/Kilo support evidence, but 30.5B total/3.3B active weights. Memory depends on precision/runtime/context; 262144-token specification does not guarantee hardware fit. GPT-5/Claude equivalence and repository success remain unmeasured.

rows.name: Cursor desktop editor
rows.reason: Cursor is a separate desktop editor; official guidance migrates settings from VS Code into Cursor. This conflicts with working directly inside VS Code.

rows.name: Cline with Ollama or LM Studio
rows.reason: Cline offers coordinated VS Code edits, commands and error inspection with locally served models. Model capability and memory remain decisive; open-source extension does not make hosted inference unlimited.

rows.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
rows.reason: Open-weight coding backend documents local serving, long context and Cline tools. 30.5B total parameters and cache demand substantial memory despite 3.3B active; GPT-5/Claude parity unestablished.

rows.name: Roo (Ruby spreadsheet library)
rows.reason: The repository is a Ruby library for reading spreadsheet formats; it provides neither a VS Code AI assistant nor coding-model integration.

rows.name: Continue
rows.reason: Its open-source VS Code extension supplies agent, chat, edit and autocomplete modes, with documented local Ollama support that can avoid hosted usage allowances.

rows.name: Tabby self-hosted server and VS Code extension
rows.reason: Tabby offers self-hosted VS Code completion, code questions and inline editing. Operating a server and selecting models are required; a full autonomous multi-file workflow was not established.

rows.name: Kilo Code with its local Ollama provider
rows.reason: Kilo supports local Ollama in VS Code; set main/small models, prevent Gateway fallback. Autocomplete/version alignment remains unresolved: current guidance says Mistral BYOK or disable. Project performance untested.

rows.name: Roo (Ruby spreadsheet library)
rows.reason: The supplied project is a Ruby spreadsheet-reading gem. Its documented operation is parsing spreadsheet files, so it does not supply the requested AI coding-assistant interface inside VS Code.

rows.name: Continue with local Ollama models
rows.reason: Local chat/edit/completion documented through Ollama search excerpts. Final 2.0.0 is no longer actively maintained; maintenance isn't mandatory. Final-extension/runtime/model compatibility and full multi-file agent workflow untested.

rows.name: Aider with a local Ollama model
rows.reason: Aider with local Ollama supports project editing from VS Code's terminal when terminal-first interaction is acceptable. Native inline completion is unverified; model reliability and context sizing need evaluation.

rows.name: Cline with Ollama and a local Qwen3-Coder model
rows.reason: Cline/Ollama with local Qwen3-Coder documents coordinated VS Code edits. No firsthand run; hardware, latency and tool-call reliability remain unknown. GPT-5/Claude equivalence or reliable large-codebase performance is unproven.

rows.name: Continue
rows.reason: Official documentation identifies an open-source VS Code extension with agent, chat, edit and autocomplete features; inspected public code supports local Ollama roles. Unverified project performance warrants qualification, not exclusion.
